TWO DIFFERENT PERMISSIONS, AND THEY DISAGREE - ON PURPOSE.

 HMIControlAvailable is what the SPT base grants, and the base grants it in
 ePMLUnitMode_Manual only: FB_PackML_BaseModule.HMIPermissions leaves the
 Maintenance branch empty. It is what every cylinder in this group gates on.

 ManualRunAvailable is what THIS block's Execute actually honours, which is
 Manual OR Maintenance. A drive tile must gate its Run buttons on this one,
 or the buttons would grey out in Maintenance while the PLC still obeys them.

Running is what the drive was commanded to do, Active is what it reports
 back from the twin's motion observer. Commanded and not active is a dropped
 contactor - which is why both are published rather than just the command.

The same value as text, so a tile can show it without converting

Bypassed: the group this unit serves is not available, so the unit fixes the
 pallet and releases it again without ever raising ReadyForOperation. Routed in
 from the group by the Machine module - the unit does not decide this itself.

--- Ring handshake -----------------------------------------------------
 Ready: idle and empty, will accept a pallet.
 Occupied: holding a pallet. Deliberately not called Busy - the base FB
 already uses Busy to mean "mid async operation", which is something else.

--- Functional group handshake -----------------------------------------
 ReadyForOperation: pallet stopped AND lifted, the group may run.
 OperationDone: the group has reported finished.

Contact polarity. FALSE against the twin, which reports TRUE while pressed.
 TRUE for real hardware, where an emergency stop is normally-closed and reads
 TRUE while healthy. Surfaced on the panel because getting it wrong is
 invisible and dangerous - see _docs/reference/plc-io-exceptions.md.

TRUE while pressed. On the emergency stops this means LATCHED - the twin's
 mushrooms are Toggle type, so a click holds until clicked again.

The lamp as the PLC is driving it this scan. Solid while latched, flashing
 while latched during Clearing - the owning module decides, not this device.

How long the lock has to confirm after being commanded before fault 1 is
 raised. Writable from the panel: a sticky lock on a demo cell is exactly the
 kind of thing tuned against the running machine.

The two bits that matter, and they are NOT redundant: a door can be shut
 without being locked, and that is precisely the state that must not let
 Production start.
0 none, 1 lock commanded but never confirmed within LockTime.
TRUE while the PLC is commanding this lock engaged - Production only.

Closed AND Locked. Published as its own bit so a panel shows the same
 verdict the safety chain uses instead of ANDing two lamps by eye.

Half period of the flash clock. Writable from the panel, which is the only
 practical way to tune a blink rate against a running machine.

The shared flash phase, for a panel that wants to blink something in step
 with the tower rather than run its own clock.

The four lamps exactly as the coils are being driven this scan - already
 blended, so a flashing lamp reads TRUE/FALSE at the flash rate and a panel
 bound to these mirrors the real tower without re-deriving anything.

The conditions behind the lamps, so a panel can say WHY a lamp is lit
 instead of leaving the operator to infer it from a colour. Amber and blue
 have no source in this machine yet and stay FALSE - see
 _docs/reference/state-lamp.md.

--- HMI ----------------------------------------------------------------
 One struct for the whole tile, extending the SPT module interface. The
 inherited half is bridged to the base's own PackMLBaseModule_HMI in two
 places: HMICommunication pushes Command in before the base acts on it,
 PublishHMI copies Config and Status back out after. The Station half is this
 block's own and is filled by PublishHMI alone.
